translation.english_text: Father, why is no one here? Where is he, father?...
Oh, oh! In such a hurry already? Once the leaf is laid out, would they fail to serve the rice? Come, girl, come......
notes: The meal-leaf/rice metaphor is preserved as source rhetoric.

translation.english_text: Yes... all the arrangements for the wedding...

Are you looking around thinking there are no drums, no wedding pavilion, no feast?... This is only the bride's house. The muhurtham will take place elsewhere. Besides... this wedding has to happen without Sukhadev knowing about it...
notes: `முகூர்த்தம்` is retained as `muhurtham` for the ritual wedding moment.

translation.english_text: Yes.... yes... that Sukhadev...
[Tirisangu sees Sukhadev arriving.]

source_locator.description: After seeing Sukhadev arrive, Tirisangu turns the interrupted description into a face-saving remark to Muthayi.

translation.english_text: You say he is very handsome—someone you like very much......
notes: The source prints no speaker label for this line; Tirisangu attribution remains derivative provenance only.

translation.english_text: Father... what are you babbling about!...

source_locator.description: Muthayi turns, sees Sukhadev and faints.

translation.english_text: [She turns, sees Sukhadev and faints.]
What?... what?...
Nothing... nothing... The shock of seeing you made her faint... the heart pounds from happiness, does it not, brother?...
notes: Frozen spacing in `ஒன்றுமில்ல ை` is not treated as a source correction.

translation.english_text: Yes!... yes! Mine too is pounding just like that now...
All right; you go upstairs. I will come later.

source_locator.description: Sukhadev leaves; Muthayi recovers and Tirisangu displays costly jewels and clothes.

translation.english_text: [Sukhadev leaves. Muthayi recovers from her faint and rises. Tirisangu shows her costly jewels and clothes.]
Muthayi! Look at these... ornaments set with pearls, coral, gems and diamonds! Shining silk!... glittering diamond! Precious gem! Ah... ha... all these....
A price that pleases your heart! A net cast over your daughter!...
notes: Frozen `தாப்படும்` is rendered from the immediate price/net contrast without changing the Tamil source.

translation.english_text: Listen to what I say...

Do not say anything. I understand everything now. The very shell brings the pearl and drops it in the mud!... The red-lotus creeper itself plucks off its petals and gives them to the buffalo! Father, would you plot like this against your own daughter?!...

english_page_segments.english_text: Do not say anything. I understand everything now. The very shell brings the pearl and drops it in the mud
!... The red-lotus creeper itself plucks off its petals and gives them to the buffalo! Father, would you plot like this against your own daughter?!...

notes: The immutable source record prints speaker label `திரி`, even though the rhetoric addresses `அப்பா`; English preserves the record ownership and does not relabel the Tamil evidence.

translation.english_text: Daughter!... If you were a daughter, would you let a father's heart burn like this? If you were truly a daughter—an aged father—a loving father—a man who has suffered many days in poverty—now thinks he might finally live a little, would you not think of helping him?... To let me live, am I asking you to jump into a fire? Am I asking for some great sacrifice?.... A position impossible to find... he says he will place you there and worship you as its goddess... yet you sob, heave and lament, foolish girl! I have fulfilled so many wishes of yours; can you not fulfil this first and last wish of mine?....
Many times I have given you tender coconuts; what difference is there, father, between what you are saying and a coconut tree saying, 'Just once, I will fall on your head'?...
notes: The coconut-tree analogy and its reversal of parent-child obligation are preserved literally.

translation.english_text: Tch, insolent chatterbox! Keep quiet! In the morning you and the prince are to be married!... Get yourself ready for it...

source_locator.description: Tirisangu leaves quickly and sees Vedalam outside.

translation.english_text: [He leaves quickly. As he comes outside, he sees Vedalam.]
Come... you have arrived at a good time...
What, Tirisangu? How are all my arrangements......
All the arrangements are fine! There is just one flaw.
What is it?
Muthayi refuses to marry Sukhadev...
That's a fine thing! It is like saying the meal is ready but there is no rice! What, man... earlier you said the two of them were lovers united as one...
notes: Frozen spacing in `இல்ல ை` is not normalized in the Tamil evidence.

translation.english_text: Muthayi is a stubborn girl. I cannot change her obstinacy... You must somehow...
Hm... I will try... Where is she now?
She is inside.
All right, all of you come; I will set her right myself!...
notes: Frozen `நீங்கள் யாரும் வாருங்கள்` is translated without silently changing the source despite the following action showing Vedalam entering alone.

source_locator.description: Vedalam goes inside and addresses Muthayi.

translation.english_text: [Vedalam goes inside. Seeing Muthayi, he speaks.]

Foolish girl! Get up! Why are you sitting like this?... Won't you speak?... Hm... this is exactly the time that is slipping away... the sea is roaring... and you are sitting on a catamaran singing an oppari!... Ah! Look to what must be done, dear girl! Crying cannot ward off danger...... Why are you crying?
notes: `ஒப்பாரி` is retained as `oppari`, a lament form.
The frozen phrase around `தகப்பன் இது தான் நேரம் போவிருக்கிறது` is translated conservatively from immediate context and is not repaired in Tamil.

translation.english_text: The town laughs; I cry...
True. Yet, tender-hearted maiden! Realize that there is still a chance to escape this turmoil...
A chance to escape!...
Yes... a chance indeed... your liberation... the sign that your suffering is departing has come in the form of Vedalam...
What are you saying?....

You do not know how affectionately Muthan and I have lived as friends... the gold you gave, Sumathi swallowed and kept... Muthan was locked in the camp prison... I gave the wealth I had saved with great hardship over many days and have now freed him.

english_page_segments.english_text: You do not know how affectionately Muthan and I have lived as friends... the gold you gave, Sumathi swallowed and kept... Muthan was locked in the camp prison... I gave the wealth I had saved with great hardship over many days

notes: Frozen source `பொண்ணு` is interpreted from the immediate money plot as the gold/money Muthayi had sent; the Tamil evidence is not changed.

translation.english_text: Ah!... Has my Muthan been freed?

Alas, pitiable girl!... Hear more happy news. I came to know that your father is cruel and arranged this marriage by deceiving you... so I ran here at once to save you!... I have come like a wedding guest, trying to free my friend's beloved.
Sir! May you live for many years!
Why should I live long in this unjust world, girl? Never mind that... Listen, young bird!... Muthan will come here tonight; leave with him.
Will he come?...
Would he fail to come?... Be careful, both of you!

source_locator.description: Vedalam leaves and Muthan enters the room disguised as an old man.

translation.english_text: [Vedalam leaves. Muthan enters the room disguised as an old man.]
Aththan! Vedalam said you would come.
notes: `அத்தான்` is retained as `Aththan`, the intimate kinship/address term used by Muthayi for Muthan.

translation.english_text: Vedalam! He is a venomous snake! Muthayi, somehow you must make Sukhadev come here.
notes: Exact source label `முத்` is preserved; context identifies this speech as Muthan without rewriting the label.

translation.english_text: Sukhadev? Why?
notes: Exact source label `முத்` is preserved; context identifies this reply as Muthayi.

translation.english_text: Do you know why? For us to leave now is no ordinary matter; danger is waiting all around us!
notes: Exact source label `முத்` is preserved; context identifies this speech as Muthan.

source_locator.description: Tirisangu comes in and Muthan hides.

translation.english_text: [Tirisangu comes in. Muthan hides.]
Muthayi! Still not asleep?...
I cannot sleep, father!... I am deep in thought.
What are you thinking about, girl?...
That Vedalam came and put sense into me... all these days I had lost my wits and trusted that Muthan...
My daughter! Is it really you speaking?... Ah! Vedalam was right... Muthayi, only now do I feel I have gained the benefit of having you as my daughter...
Father, will you do me a favour?...
I will do a thousand; tell me!
In the morning Sukhadev and I are to be married. Now I want to meet him and speak about a few things! My heart too is longing to see him...
My darling daughter!... Is that such a great matter? I will send him right now...

source_locator.description: Tirisangu leaves quickly; Muthan whispers the plan to Muthayi and leaves.

translation.english_text: [Tirisangu leaves quickly. Muthan tells Muthayi the secret plan and leaves.]

source_locator.description: Tirisangu goes to Sukhadev and tells him of Muthayi's eagerness.

translation.english_text: [Tirisangu goes to Sukhadev and tells him of Muthayi's eagerness.]

Ah! My goddess of love! Here I come. Can fire and cotton remain still when brought close together? Uncle! You can go and sleep soundly—I will not let Muthayi sleep tonight—I am going to keep talking to her!...
notes: The fire/cotton erotic metaphor is preserved rather than euphemized.

source_locator.description: Sukhadev comes to where Muthayi is.

translation.english_text: [Sukhadev comes to where Muthayi is.]
My dear! Why did you call me? Oh! Won't you speak? Are you this shy?...
I need to discuss something.
Discuss something? A lover and beloved—this bedchamber is a pavilion of sensual delight, not a place for discussing news, my dear!...
notes: The source's sexual innuendo is translated without euphemizing it.

translation.english_text: You must not make all these jokes...
What do you want to talk about? Speak!...
What is your opinion about equality between men and women?
Half man—half woman—my principle is that men and women should be created as Ardhanarishvaras themselves—if I were God, that is exactly how I would make them!...
notes: `அர்த்தநாரீஸ்வரர்கள்` is retained as `Ardhanarishvaras`, preserving the source's religious image rather than replacing it with an abstract equality term.

translation.english_text: Ah... you have stated a vast and complicated matter so briefly!... The woman fortunate enough to attain you is lucky indeed—I want to ask one more thing.
notes: Frozen spacing in `உங்களேஅடை யும்` is not used to alter the Tamil source.

translation.english_text: Do not ask all these things retail—ask wholesale!
notes: The `சில்லறை` / `மொத்தமாக` retail/wholesale wordplay is preserved.

translation.english_text: If I ask it, you cannot answer immediately. We have to talk for a long time.
We will talk—never mind—what other pleasure do I have except talking with you!
What a lovely moon—shall the two of us go toward the riverbank and talk of pleasant stories?
notes: Frozen `சுவையான க்கதைகள்` is translated contextually without changing the Tamil record.

translation.english_text: Ah!... You have said the long thing—come, let us set out, my dear!...
notes: Frozen `நீண்டதைச் சொன்னாய்` is retained semantically close to its printed form rather than silently normalized to a more expected phrase.

translation.english_text: Shh... do not touch... all that is for tomorrow! Come, let us go...
I am ready...
You say men and women are equal—then you in women's clothes, and I in men's...
Oh no, in women's clothes?
See! Being a woman means degradation...
No... no... it is not that; I would feel shy if the men saw me...
We are going secretly so no one will know, are we not? When you and I are one life in two bodies, what is wrong in your wearing my clothes and my wearing yours?...

english_page_segments.english_text: We are going secretly so no one will know, are we not? When you and I are one life in two bodies, what is wrong in your wearing my clothes and my

translation.english_text: There is nothing wrong, my golden treasure! I will do exactly as you say...

source_locator.description: Sukhadev appears in women's clothes and Muthayi in men's clothes; Velazhagan's soldiers are hidden nearby.

translation.english_text: [Sukhadev appears in women's clothes and Muthayi in men's clothes. Velazhagan's soldiers are hidden nearby.]
My jewel, Muthayi! What a sweet moment!... What a wonderful sight!... Ah! To have you beside me... alas, I do not even understand where we are going!...
You will not understand... you will not!... You... must come without speaking.

source_locator.description: The soldiers mistake Sukhadev for Muthayi, attack and carry him away; Muthayi remains, and Muthan comes from behind and startles her.

translation.english_text: [The soldiers mistake Sukhadev for Muthayi, attack him and carry him away. Muthayi remains. Muthan comes up from behind and startles her.]
Hey! Who is that?...
[They both laugh.]
So—that is done. What is our next plan?
The next plan? Give me your ring like this... up... put it on the finger!... Here!... stretch out your finger...
notes: `கணையாழி` is rendered as `ring` from the exchange-of-rings action that follows.

source_locator.description: Muthan puts his ring on Muthayi's finger.

translation.english_text: [He puts his ring on her finger.]
What is this?...
When two lovers are of one mind, exchanging rings itself is marriage...
All right... we are married now... what next?...
From now on... f... f... we have to run a family...
notes: The source stammer `கு...கு...குடும்பம்` is retained through an English stammer rather than smoothed away.

translation.english_text: Run a family right here in the forest?...

Why not?... Did Rama and Sita not live in the forest for fourteen years? When a man and woman are alone, there is no dwelling more delightful than forest-dwelling... Look at the peacock dancing in joy! Look at the cuckoo singing melody to the ear's fill! Look at the river!—look at the waterfall!—look at its beauty!—come a little nearer and look!

english_page_segments.english_text: Why not?... Did Rama and Sita not live in the forest for fourteen years? When a man and woman are alone, there is no dwelling more delightful than forest-dwelling
... Look at the peacock dancing in joy! Look at the cuckoo singing melody to the ear's fill! Look at the river!—look at the waterfall!—look at its beauty!—come a little nearer and look!

notes: The repeated `வாசம்` in the forest-dwelling line carries wordplay that cannot be reproduced exactly in English; the residence sense is preserved.

translation.english_text: Hm...
Rama must have spoken to Sita like that... Would forest life have been bitter for them?... It may have been bitter for Lakshmana... poor man, married yet a brahmachari!
notes: `பிரமச்சாரி` is retained as `brahmachari` to preserve the comic cultural reference.

translation.english_text: Mischief!
All right, Muthayi, come! We must live hidden in disguise... otherwise Velazhagan will somehow catch us... come... come!...
